---
title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

Calling `await navigation()` keeps runtime work below it out of the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and per-link prefetches. description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

---
title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.
nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Learn more about the APIs and concepts used in this guide.
  links:
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching

    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

title: instant
description: Configure instant navigation validation for a route segment.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
  links:

---

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

00002| title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
00003| nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
00004| description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
00005| related:
00006|   title: Next Steps

00008|   links:

00013| ---
00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00088| 
00089| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00090| 
00091| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
00092| 
00093| ```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
00094| import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
00095| import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099| 
00100|   await instant(page, async () => {
00101|     const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()
00103|     await link.click()
00104|     await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
00105| 
00106|     await expect(
00107|       page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00108|     ).toBeVisible()
00109|     await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
00110|   })
00111| })
00112| ```
00113| 
00114| Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
00115| 
00116| ### Static or cached content
00117| 
00118| The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:
00119| 
00120| ```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
00121| // Before
00122| <Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
00123| // After
00124| <Link href="/about">About</Link>
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| ### Uncached content
00128| 
00129| Cache it with `use cache` so it gets included in the App Shell, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00130| 
00131| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher

00133| export default async function Page() {
00134|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00135|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00136| }
00137| ```
00138| 
00139| ```jsx filename="app/products/page.js" switcher
00140| // Before

00142|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00143|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00144| }
00145| ```
00146| 
00147| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher

00149| async function getProducts() {
00150|   'use cache'
00151|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00152|   return res.json()
00153| }
00154| 
00155| export default async function Page() {
00156|   return <ProductList products={await getProducts()} />
00157| }
00158| ```
00159| 
00160| ```jsx filename="app/products/page.js" switcher

00173| > **Good to know**: The App Shell carries cached content whose [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes, which holds for the `default` profile used above and every preset except `seconds`. Shorter-lived content streams in after the navigation instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior).
00174| 
00175| ### Session content
00176| 
00177| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. Read the session value outside the cached function and pass it in, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00178| 
00179| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00180| // Before
00181| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00182| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00183| 
00184| async function TeamTopics() {
00185|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00186|   const topics = await db.topics.forTeam(team)
00187|   return <TopicList topics={topics} />
00188| }
00189| 
00190| export default function Page() {
00191|   return (
00192|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00193|       <TeamTopics />
00194|     </Suspense>
00195|   )
00196| }
00197| ```
00198| 
00199| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00200| // Before
00201| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00202| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00203| 
00204| async function TeamTopics() {
00205|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00206|   const topics = await db.topics.forTeam(team)

00210| export default function Page() {

00212|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00213|       <TeamTopics />

00215|   )

00221| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00222| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00223| 
00224| async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) {
00225|   'use cache'
00226|   return db.topics.forTeam(team)

00230|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00231|   return <TopicList topics={await getTopics(team)} />
00232| }

00239|   )

00242|

00266| 
00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00288| 
00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00294|     snippets={[
00295|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00296|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00297|     ]}
00298|   />
00299|   <FixCard
00300|     group="disable"
00301|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00302|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00303|     snippets={[
00304|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00306|       { text: '</Link>' },
00307|     ]}
00308|   />
00309| </FixCardGrid>
00310| 
00311| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00312| 
00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00339|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {
00343|      return <Dashboard />
00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00351| 
00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00353| 
00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00356| ```
00357| 
00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00361| 
00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00365| 
00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00370|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"
00371|     snippets={[
00372|       { text: '<Suspense fallback={…}>', highlight: true },
00373|       { text: '  <Details params={params} />' },

00376|   />

00378|     group="block"
00379|     title="Allow blocking route"
00380|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00381|     snippets={[

00383|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00384|     ]}
00385|   />

00393| // Before - awaiting params at the top ties the App Shell to one URL

00395|   const { slug } = await params
00396|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00397|   return (
00398|     <ProductLayout>
00399|       <Details product={product} />
00400|     </ProductLayout>
00401|   )
00402| }
00403| ```
00404| 
00405| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00409|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00410|   return (
00411|     <ProductLayout>
00412|       <Details product={product} />
00413|     </ProductLayout>
00414|   )
00415| }
00416| ```
00417| 
00418| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00419| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00420| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00421| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {

00425|     <ProductLayout>
00426|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00427|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00428|       </Suspense>
00429|     </ProductLayout>
00430|   )
00431| }
00432| ```
00433| 
00434| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00435| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00436| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00437| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00438| 
00439| export default function Page({ params }) {
00440|   return (
00441|     <ProductLayout>
00442|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00443|         <ProductDetails params={params} />

00445|     </ProductLayout>
00446|   )

00450| The child awaits the promise inside the boundary:
00451| 
00452| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher

00455| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {

00471| 
00472| > **Good to know**: A `params` or `searchParams` read inside [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) surfaces as [URL data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) instead.

00474| ## Prefetching URL data
00475| 
00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) resolves it ahead of the click for links with `prefetch={true}`, at the cost of a server invocation per prefetchable link. [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00088| 
00089| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00090| 
00091| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
00092| 
00093| ```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
00094| import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
00095| import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099| 
00100|   await instant(page, async () => {
00101|     const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()
00103|     await link.click()
00104|     await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
00105| 
00106|     await expect(
00107|       page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00108|     ).toBeVisible()
00109|     await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
00110|   })
00111| })
00112| ```
00113| 
00114| Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
00115| 
00116| ### Static or cached content
00117| 
00118| The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:
00119| 
00120| ```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
00121| // Before
00122| <Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
00123| // After
00124| <Link href="/about">About</Link>
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| ### Uncached content
00128| 
00129| Cache it with `use cache` so it gets included in the App Shell, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00130| 
00131| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher
00132| // Before
00133| export default async function Page() {
00134|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00135|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00136| }
00137| ```
00138| 
00139| ```jsx filename="app/products/page.js" switcher

00141| export default async function Page() {
00142|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00143|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00144| }
00145| ```
00146| 
00147| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher
00148| // After - cached, so the App Shell carries it
00149| async function getProducts() {
00150|   'use cache'
00151|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00152|   return res.json()
00153| }
00154| 
00155| export default async function Page() {
00156|   return <ProductList products={await getProducts()} />
00157| }
00158| ```
00159| 
00160| ```jsx filename="app/products/page.js" switcher

Shorter-lived content streams in after the navigation instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior).
00174| 
00175| ### Session content
00176| 
00177| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. Read the session value outside the cached function and pass it in, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00178| 
00179| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher

00181| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00182| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00183| 
00184| async function TeamTopics() {
00185|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00186|   const topics = await db.topics.forTeam(team)
00187|   return <TopicList topics={topics} />
00188| }
00189| 
00190| export default function Page() {

00192|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00193|       <TeamTopics />
00194|     </Suspense>
00195|   )

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00288| 
00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00294|     snippets={[
00295|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00296|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00297|     ]}
00298|   />
00299|   <FixCard
00300|     group="disable"
00301|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00302|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00303|     snippets={[
00304|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00306|       { text: '</Link>' },
00307|     ]}
00308|   />
00309| </FixCardGrid>
00310| 
00311| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00312| 
00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00339|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {
00343|      return <Dashboard />
00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00351| 
00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00353| 
00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00356| ```
00357| 
00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.

00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00365| 
00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00370|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"

00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

00379|     title="Allow blocking route"
00380|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00381|     snippets={[
00382|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00383|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00384|     ]}
00385|   />

00400|     </ProductLayout>
00401|   )
00402| }
00403| ```

00433| 
00434| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00438|

---
title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch config
description: Configure how a route segment is prefetched during client navigation.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
---

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
> - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`.

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. title: Ensuring instant navigations
description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

---
title: Ensuring instant navigations
description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.
nav_title: Instant navigation
related:

  description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation.

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: How Next.js supports AI coding agents
00003| nav_title: AI Coding Agents
00004| description: Learn how Next.js helps AI coding agents use current framework guidance, inspect applications, verify changes, and report issues.
00005| related:
00006|   title: Next Steps
00007|   description: Learn more about the APIs and tools described in this guide.
00008|   links:
00009|     - app/guides/mcp
00010|     - app/getting-started/upgrading
00011|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules
00012|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentFeedback
00013|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade
00014| ---
00015| 
00016| AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00017| 
00018| For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).
00019| 
00020| <span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />
00021| 
00022| ## Version-matched documentation
00023| 
00024| Next.js 16.2 and later include documentation that matches the installed framework version. The documentation is available at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and mirrors the structure of the [Next.js documentation site](https://nextjs.org/docs):
00025| 
00026| ```txt
00027| node_modules/next/dist/docs/
00028| ├── 01-app/
00029| │   ├── 01-getting-started/
00030| │   ├── 02-guides/
00031| │   └── 03-api-reference/
00032| ├── 02-pages/
00033| ├── 03-architecture/
00034| └── index.mdx
00035| ```
00036| 
00037| The bundled copy gives coding agents access to the APIs and patterns supported by the project without a network request or external lookup. [Upgrading Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/upgrading) also updates the bundled documentation.
00038| 
00039| ### Managed documentation instructions
00040| 
00041| Next.js makes the bundled documentation discoverable through managed instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the project root. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot read this file when they start a session.
00042| 
00043| [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) creates the agent files for new projects. When `next dev` detects a coding agent, it creates or updates the managed instructions for existing projects. The block directs the agent to the documentation installed with the project:
00044| 
00045| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00046| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00047| 
00048| ## This is NOT the Next.js you know
00049| 
00050| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
00051| 
00052| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00053| 
00054| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00055| ```
00056| 
00057| Next.js updates only the content between the agent rules markers and preserves the rest of `AGENTS.md`.
00058| 
00059| [Research comparing `AGENTS.md` with knowledge Skills](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals) found a 100% pass rate with bundled documentation, compared with up to 79% for Skill-based approaches. See the current [Next.js agent evaluation results](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00060| 
00061| Managed documentation instructions are enabled by default in Next.js 16.3 and later. See the [`agentRules` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules) to configure or disable them.
00062| 
00063| ### Version support
00064| 
00065| Next.js 16.3 and later include bundled documentation and support managed agent instructions. Next.js 16.2 includes the bundled documentation but does not generate instructions automatically.
00066| 
00067| Next.js 16.1 and earlier do not include the bundled documentation. The legacy `agents-md` command downloads a version-matched copy to `.next-docs/` and indexes it in `AGENTS.md`:
00068| 
00069| ```bash
00070| npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
00071| ```
00072| 
00073| ### Docs over the network
00074| 
00075| The Next.js documentation is also available as Markdown over the network for agents that fetch pages instead of reading `node_modules`. Every page on [nextjs.org/docs](https://nextjs.org/docs) has a plain Markdown version at its `.md` URL, and clients that send an `Accept: text/markdown` header receive Markdown. This includes the per-error pages under `/docs/messages`, which are not bundled.
00076| 
00077| The index at [`/docs/llms.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt) and the single-file [`/docs/llms-full.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms-full.txt) follow the [`llms.txt` convention](https://llmstxt.org/), so agents that already read `llms.txt` for other tools can discover the Next.js docs the same way.
00078| 
00079| ## Automatic agent feedback
00080| 
00081| Automatic agent feedback lets coding agents keep track of potential Next.js issues without interrupting the current user request. Before the final response, the agent evaluates those issues and opens each qualifying report in a separate review form in your default browser.
00082| 
00083| Before opening a form, the agent attempts to anonymize the report by replacing customer and project details with generic descriptions and omitting source code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, and personal information. Review the draft and remove anything you don't want to include. Nothing is sent until you select **Send feedback**.
00084| 
00085| With the option enabled, `next dev` adds the following managed feedback instructions to the agent file when it detects an AI coding agent:
00086| 
00087| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00088| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00089| 
00090| ## Report Next.js feedback
00091| 
00092| The project owner enabled `experimental.agentFeedback`, authorizing this feedback pass. When enabled, `next dev` writes this block and restores it if removed. Commit `AGENTS.md` with your work to keep the tree clean.
00093| 
00094| During the current user request, retain anonymized facts as feedback candidates for meaningful or recurring Next.js issues:
00095| 
00096| - Crashes, hangs, OOMs, or unexpected slowness
00097| - Incorrect behavior, output, errors, or diagnostics
00098| - Missing, unclear, or conflicting documentation
00099| - Unexpected CLI, codemod, Skill, or upgrade behavior and non-obvious workarounds
00100| 
00101| Continue the current user request without reporting immediately. Routine debugging is not feedback. Verify changes before retaining them as feedback candidates. Never retain code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, personal information, or project-specific data.
00102| 
00103| Before the final response, run one reporting pass. If candidates remain, from this file's directory run `node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next internal agent-feedback-instructions` once without piping or truncating its output. Follow its output or error guidance. If a network sandbox blocks it, retry with network access; if it still returns no output, continue normally.
00104| 
00105| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00106| ```
00107| 
00108| Next.js updates only the content between the agent feedback markers and preserves the rest of the file.
00109| 
00110| Automatic agent feedback is experimental, disabled by default, and available only when [Next.js Telemetry](/telemetry) is enabled. It does not run in CI. See the [`agentFeedback` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentFeedback) to enable it.
00111| 
00112| ## Agent-guided upgrades
00113| 
00114| `next upgrade --agent` checks for an available upgrade, gathers the version-matched migration guides, and hands the task to a coding agent. The agent applies the changes and verifies the app:
00115| 
00116| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00117| npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
00118| ```
00119| 
00120| The experimental [`agentUpgrade`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade) option shows security upgrade reminders during `next dev` and `next build` by default. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for the available policies and workflow.
00121| 
00122| <span id="step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility" />
00123| 
00124| ## Runtime visibility
00125| 
00126| Agents need both framework and browser state to verify a running application. Next.js and its supporting tools expose these complementary views as structured text.
00127| 
00128| First, `next dev` forwards browser console errors and warnings to the terminal (the [`logging.browserToTerminal`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging) config), so the output agents already read carries the client-side failures they're asked to fix.
00129| 
00130| `next dev` also writes its PID, port, and URL to `.next/dev/lock`. If you run `next dev` while another development server is already running for the project, the command prints the existing server's URL and PID, along with a command to stop it. Continue with the existing server when possible to avoid interrupting the active development session.
00131| 
00132| The **framework's view** comes from the [Next.js MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) at `/_next/mcp`, which exposes the running dev server's routes, server logs, and compilation issues. Its `get_compilation_issues` and `compile_route` tools report whether the code compiles straight from the dev server, so an agent doesn't have to run a full `next build` to find out.
00133| 
00134| The [`next-dev-loop` skill](#next-dev-loop) adds the **browser's view** through [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser), a CLI that exposes the DOM, console, network, and Web Vitals as structured text. The Skill opens `agent-browser` with React DevTools enabled, which also exposes the component tree and pending Suspense boundaries. An agent can run a command such as `react tree` and use the structured output to decide what to inspect next.
00135| 
00136| Together with the Next.js MCP server, `next-dev-loop` combines the framework's and the browser's perspectives into one edit-and-verify loop.
00137| 
00138| <span id="step-3-let-errors-drive-the-fixes" />
00139| 
00140| ## Built-in guidance for errors
00141| 
00142| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) enabled, a blocking error presents labeled fixes, each making a different trade-off. The dev overlay adds a **Copy prompt** button that packages the chosen fix into a paste-ready prompt. The prompt walks the agent through reading the matching error page, applying the canonical pattern, and verifying the result at runtime.
00143| 
00144| The same menu prints in the `next dev` terminal and in `next build` output, so an agent reading CI logs sees it too:
00145| 
00146| ```txt filename="Terminal"
00147| Route "/products/[slug]": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering.
00148| 
00149| `fetch(...)` or `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route
00150| from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience.
00151| 
00152| Ways to fix this:
00153|   - [stream] Provide a placeholder with `<Suspense fallback={...}>` around the data access
00154|   - [cache] Cache the data access with `"use cache"` (does not apply to `connection()`)
00155|   - [block] Set `export const instant = false` to allow a blocking route
00156| 
00157| Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic
00158|     at ProductPage (app/products/[slug]/page.tsx:52:32)
00159|     ...
00160| ```
00161| 
00162| `next dev` shows all validation errors with source-mapped stacks in the overlay and terminal. Production builds minify server code and stop after a route fails. Use [`next build --debug-prerender`](/docs/app/guides/building#debug-prerender-errors) to enable server source maps and continue checking other routes.
00163| 
00164| The `Learn more` link resolves to a per-error page under [`/docs/messages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic) written for agents to read. Each page follows the same shape, with the canonical patterns for every fix, the trade-offs against the other fixes, and the gotchas an agent is likely to miss on a first attempt. The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#ai-workflow) walks through the full loop an agent runs on these errors, from reading the insight to writing an `instant()` test that fails before the fix and passes once it's in place.
00165| 
00166| <span id="step-4-hand-multi-step-workflows-to-skills" />
00167| 
00168| ## Skills for multi-step workflows
00169| 
00170| Framework knowledge comes from the bundled docs, not from Skills. [Benchmark results](https://nextjs.org/evals) show that always-available context outperforms on-demand retrieval. Skills cover the tasks that are workflows rather than lookups, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app. Next.js Skills package these as structured instructions an agent installs and follows, sequencing the work and pointing at the relevant docs and [runtime tooling](#runtime-visibility) along the way.
00171| 
00172| You can [browse the source for these Skills](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills) in the Next.js repository and [find them on skills.sh](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js).
00173| 
00174| The Skills serve three different workflow types:
00175| 
00176| - **Runtime foundations** such as `next-dev-loop` give any coding task a repeatable inspect, edit, and verify cycle.
00177| - **Interactive workflows** make broader changes with user checkpoints, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app.
00178| - **Unattended loops** work toward a verifiable goal and stop only for genuine decisions.
00179| 
00180| ### `next-dev-loop`
00181| 
00182| The [`next-dev-loop`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop) runtime foundation verifies changes against a running dev server using the [MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) and browser.
00183| 
00184| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00185| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop
00186| ```
00187| 
00188| Then give the agent this prompt:
00189| 
00190| ```prompt
00191| After every edit, verify the page still works at runtime using the next-dev-loop Skill.
00192| ```
00193| 
00194| ### `next-bundle-optimizer`
00195| 
00196| The [`next-bundle-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-bundle-optimizer) skill uses Turbopack's bundle analyzer to identify sources of large client-side bundles that impact your site's initial load performance.
00197| 
00198| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00199| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer
00200| ```
00201| 
00202| In audit-only mode, it produces a report without making any changes:
00203| 
00204| ```prompt

00241| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer
00242| ```
00243| 
00244| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00245| 
00246| ```prompt

00248| ```
00249| 
00250| ### `next-partial-prefetching-adoption`
00251| 
00252| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) Skill moves an app onto [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), where links share one App Shell:

00272| The [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) Skill takes a target navigation or set of navigations and works toward the UI you want ready before each click:

00281| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer
00282| ```

AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).

For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).

<span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />
